name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+6 PVI) plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Bill Keating running with a large cash advantage over Tyler MacAllister
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 96%
No general-election polls, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Keating's incumbency and fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point the same way, with no contrary evidence in polls, ratings, or headlines. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about 19 points.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong GOP environment shift could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about six points. He has raised roughly $422,000 and holds about $496,000 on hand, far outpacing Republican Tyler MacAllister, who has raised about $175,000 with only $35,000 available. No independent spending has been reported on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 96%. The national environment also favors Democrats this cycle. All available evidence points to a comfortable Keating victory, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
